LAYOUT SPEC for the old printer's press file (render as a flat, print-ready A5 PORTRAIT press PDF, trim 148 x 210 mm, no bleed, fonts embedded/subset). Per-guest menu card laid at each seat.

--- VISUAL LAYOUT (what the printed card shows) ---
Top: the OSTRA wordmark, small, centered, Bone on near-black is NOT used here; card stock is Bone #E6DFD2 with Warm-Ink text.
A GUEST LINE (large editorial serif) and a DATE LINE (small sans) beneath it.
A FIVE-COURSE LIST (editorial serif, one course per line).
A PAIRING BLOCK at the foot (small sans, a flight name + five pairing lines).

--- CRITICAL FRAME NOTE ---
The guest line, the five-course list AND the pairing block all live inside ONE FIXED-MEASURE TEXT FRAME of a set depth (approx 118 mm tall, 96 mm wide), sized by the printer to last season's SHORTER course titles. The frame does NOT auto-grow and text that runs past its depth does NOT spill to a new frame and does NOT raise an overset error at export — it simply STOPS RENDERING at the frame's bottom edge while the page still exports and the page count stays correct. The conversion exposes the whole card as a SINGLE CONTINUOUS FLOW, not four separate blocks.

assets.content:
OSTRA — how we talk about the room, and the courses spelled the way the kitchen spells them.

THE ROOM. Twenty-two seats around the pass, one seasonal tasting menu at a hundred and thirty-five dollars a head, four nights a week. Near black, spare, unhurried. One plate at a time. The photographs should feel like walking into the room, not like an advertisement. Quiet, dark, unhurried. Not a bistro and not a hotel restaurant.

FOR THE STUDIO'S DESIGNER. We need FINISHED photographs from you, not raw files. Your build is dark: near black ground, very little on the page, one plate at a time, mobile responsive. The plates have to read as one set scrolled one after another, and they also have to survive the delivery platforms, which put every picture on a WHITE card in a grid next to everybody else.

COURSE TITLES — spell them EXACTLY like this on every card (this is this season's menu):
  Course 1: Oyster, sea buckthorn, frozen cucumber
  Course 2: Georges Bank scallop, browned butter, chervil
  Course 3: Maine lobster, fennel, saffron bisque
  Course 4: Dry-aged duck, quince, elderberry
  Course 5: Sea-salt caramel, brown-butter ice cream

VARIANT SUBSTITUTIONS (keep the same spelling):
  Pescatarian: Course 4 becomes 'Georges Bank halibut, fennel, brown butter'
  Vegetarian:  Course 3 becomes 'Charred hispi cabbage, caper, brown butter'; Course 4 becomes 'Roasted celeriac, quince, hazelnut'

PAIRING FLIGHTS: 'Cellar', 'Reserve Cellar', 'Zero-Proof'. A guest with no flight gets no pairing block — do not leave a blank line where the flight would be.

A note on the words: it is 'browned butter' on the scallop and 'brown-butter' on the caramel. Yes, on purpose. Spell them as written.
assets.defect_engineered: clean support asset; the authoritative kitchen spelling of the five course titles and the variant substitutions the cards are verified against (including the deliberate 'browned butter' vs 'brown-butter')

assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, shot at a raking angle under a single warm tungsten source, of a small SUBDUED-BRASS plate mounted at the end of a near-black slate tasting-counter pass. BLIND-ENGRAVED into the brass (no ink and no paint: the mark is cut into the metal and reads only as a thin bright highlight along one edge of each stroke and a soft shadow inside the incised channel) is a compound house mark: the wordmark 'OSTRA' in a quiet editorial serif with fine hairline serifs and small tight letter counters, and beside it a small SEPARATE incised oyster-shell device with fine radiating fan lines. The raking light falls off across the plate so the right and lower half sits in soft shadow where the engraved strokes and the brass run close together in value. Aged brass with faint patina and fine surface scratches, warm tungsten glow, a real-world snapshot rather than a studio shot, no other text, no reflected room.
assets.defect_engineered: the mark carries NO ink at all: it is blind engraving read only as a thin bright edge plus a shadow in each incised stroke, so a selection naming the plate or the brass returns the SUBSTRATE and a selection naming a dark mark on a light ground finds nothing; across the shadowed half the engraved strokes and the brass run close in value; it is a COMPOUND lockup so a selection naming the whole mark returns the wordmark and silently drops the small oyster device; and the hairline serifs and the fine shell fan lines hold at full canvas but close into solid strokes at the small height the mark reproduces at the top of the near-black site and foil-sized on the menu card

assets.prompt: A screengrab of a DARK-MODE fine-dining restaurant website on a phone, near-black background (#0E0E0F), extremely minimal: a small light serif wordmark at the top, one large moody plated-food photograph filling most of the screen with generous dark negative space around it, a single thin light-grey line of navigation, one small outlined 'Reserve' button, spare light serif type. Clean, unhurried, editorial, no brand names, no real restaurant identity, generic placeholder wordmark, the kind of dark site a restaurateur would screengrab as a mood and proportion reference. CRITICAL: absolutely no real brand names, logos, wordmarks, trademarks or trade dress anywhere; the placeholder wordmark at the top MUST be an ABSTRACT, non-dictionary, invented mark (a neutral geometric glyph or nonsense letterform) that does NOT spell any real word, restaurant name, or company name — in particular do NOT render 'lumen' or any actual English word; the site carries ONLY the fictional brand OSTRA or an abstract non-word placeholder, no real restaurant identity, no famous-brand or real-restaurant look-alikes anywhere in the mock UI; no burned-in real person names, captions, or bylines.
assets.defect_engineered: three-times RETINA phone capture (1170x2532 device px = 390x844 layout pt): the wordmark's apparent size measured off it and matched 1:1 lands the recovered mark BELOW the height its serifs hold on the near-black ground; and the proportion shown is a single PORTRAIT phone frame, so the plate-to-ground ratio cannot be lifted straight onto the wide hero or the square booking graphic (the grammar has to be re-derived, not the ratio copied) (supplied 'roughly the feeling', not to be copied)
